title: Mapping Dual-Use Liability: Who Bears Legal Responsibility When AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Occur?

original_idea.body:
# Mapping Dual-Use Liability: Who Bears Legal Responsibility When AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Occur?

**Problem:** When GTG-1002 used Claude to conduct espionage, the legal liability question (Anthropic, the operator, the end user, the attackers) was not publicly resolved. No governance framework clearly assigns liability.

**Direction:** Analyze 3 legal frameworks (US CFAA, EU AI Act liability provisions, UK Computer Misuse Act) for how they would assign liability in an AI-assisted cyberattack equivalent to GTG-1002. For each framework, identify the liability gap where no party bears clear responsibility. Propose governance provisions to fill the gaps.

**Why it matters:** Clear liability assignment is a cornerstone of governance in every mature industry. Without it, AI labs lack legal incentives to improve safety and victims lack recourse.

**Relevant context:** GTG-1002 case; EU AI Act liability provisions; Tandfonline legal foundations of AI cybersecurity 2026.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear, specific impact chain: investigation → governance insight → policy improvement. Well-articulated why-it-matters.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Framework analysis requires research/reading, doable with structure and mentor guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Scope is somewhat bounded but could extend depending on depth of analysis required.
